# ADR-173 — A generated file that is committed is checked, not remembered (20.08.2026)

**Context.** Stage 6, the closing sweep of the Cedar Bench port. `src/app/shared/icon-usage.generated.ts` is written by
`tools/generate-icon-usage.mjs`, which scans every `app-icon` call site in `src/app` and is the
data behind `/dev/icons` — the page that answers "which icon means what here, and does any meaning
have two icons". Its own header says a stale answer is impossible *as long as the script is re-run*,
and that clause is the whole problem: nothing re-runs it and nothing notices when it was not. It
shipped stale twice during this port, both times because a repaint moved call sites and the file
kept describing the arrangement before the move.

The repository already answers this question everywhere else it arises. `SchemaDriftGuardTests`
fails `dotnet test` when `Entities.cs` moves without a migration; `DesignTokenDriftTests` fails when
the blog's copy of the palette falls behind `styles.scss`; `UiInventoryDriftTests` fails when a page
component has no inventory row. CLAUDE.md states the principle on the first of them — *trust it
instead of remembering*. The icon inventory was the one generated artifact left on memory.

The other two generated artifacts differ and do not need this. `icon-data.generated.ts` is derived
from the Phosphor package rather than from our own source, so it moves only when a dependency is
deliberately upgraded; `DesignTokens.generated.cs` already has `DesignTokenDriftTests`.

**Decision.**

1. **The generator gains a `--check` mode**: it renders exactly what it would write, compares it to
   the committed file, writes nothing, and exits non-zero on any difference, naming the command that
   fixes it. Rendering and checking share one code path, so the check cannot measure something other
   than what the write produces — a second implementation of the scan, in another language, would
   be a second source of truth and the drift would move rather than go.
2. **It runs as a phase of `cedar test`**, beside the contrast and density contracts, under
   `npm run check:icons`. Those two are the existing shape for "a static read of our own source that
   goes red on a defect no unit test can see", and this is the third of them.
3. **It is not a vitest spec.** The check reads the file tree, and the Angular unit-test builder
   does not serve `node:fs` to a spec; a guard that has to be argued into its own runner is a guard
   that gets deleted.

**Consequence.** Regenerating is now a step nobody has to remember: the phase names the fix in its
own failure message, and a repaint that moves call sites goes red in the same run that made it. The
cost is one more phase in the default `cedar test`, which reads the tree twice — measured at well
under a second, against a defect that reached production twice in one port.
